description: An interactive sequencing tool for Grade 7 Science (NCERT Chapter 3). Seven step cards are displayed in shuffled order. Each card describes one step in the path of electric current through a simple circuit: (1) Current starts at positive terminal of cell, (2) flows through wire to lamp, (3) enters lamp through metal case terminal, (4) passes through filament which glows, (5) exits through metal tip terminal, (6) flows back through wire, (7) returns to negative terminal — loop complete. Students drag cards into the correct numbered slots (1-7). Visual feedback: correct placement shows green border and number. Incorrect shows red shake. When all 7 are correct, an animated current flow arrow traces the complete loop with a celebration effect. Optional hints toggle. Blue theme colour for circuit/electricity. Indian school context. Clean card-based UI with touch-friendly drag-and-drop. Numbers shown on slots.

led_circuit_sequence.description: LED circuit variant — current must flow in correct direction through LED

additionalProps.title: Trace Current in an LED Circuit
additionalProps.subtitle: NCERT Grade 7 · Section 3.2.4
additionalProps.instructionText: Arrange the steps for current flow in an LED circuit. Remember: LED only works in one direction!

steps.label: Current starts at positive terminal (+) of the battery
Current flows through wire to the LED
Current enters the longer wire (positive terminal) of LED
Current passes through the LED — it glows!
Current exits through the shorter wire (negative terminal) of LED
Current flows back through the return wire
Current returns to negative terminal (−) of the battery

additionalProps.completionMessage: Great work! Remember: LED only allows current in ONE direction — positive to negative!
additionalProps.hintText: 💡 Hint: LED has a longer wire (+) and shorter wire (−). Current enters from the positive side!

water_pipe_analogy_sequence.description: Water pipe analogy for understanding circuits

additionalProps.title: Water Pipe Analogy for Circuits
additionalProps.subtitle: Understanding electricity using water flow
additionalProps.instructionText: Arrange the water pipe analogy steps to understand how electric current works!

steps.label: Water pump pushes water (like the cell pushes current)
Water flows through pipe to the water wheel (like wire to lamp)
Water turns the wheel (like current lights the lamp)
Water flows back through return pipe (like return wire)
Water returns to the pump — loop complete!

additionalProps.completionMessage: Just like water in pipes, electricity flows in a complete loop!
additionalProps.hintText: 💡 Hint: Think of the cell as a water pump — where does the water start?

switch_circuit_sequence.description: Circuit with switch — includes switch ON step

additionalProps.title: Current Flow with a Switch
additionalProps.subtitle: NCERT Grade 7 · Section 3.2.6
additionalProps.instructionText: Trace the path of current in a circuit that has a switch. What happens when the switch is ON?

steps.label: Current starts at positive terminal (+) of the cell
Current flows through wire to the switch
Switch is ON — safety pin touches both drawing pins, completing the path
Current flows through wire to the lamp
Current passes through the filament — lamp glows!
Current flows back through the return wire
Current returns to negative terminal (−) — loop complete!

additionalProps.completionMessage: The switch completes or breaks the circuit. When ON, current flows and the lamp glows!
additionalProps.hintText: 💡 Hint: The switch comes BEFORE the lamp in this circuit!

agentReadme.overview: Interactive sequencing tool for Grade 7 Science (NCERT Chapter 3 — Electricity: Circuits and their Components). Students arrange 7 shuffled step cards into the correct order showing the path of electric current through a simple circuit. Drag-and-drop with visual feedback (green for correct, red shake for incorrect). Celebration animation on completion. Supports customisation via additionalProps for different circuit types (LED, switch circuits, water analogy, etc.).

If a student gets stuck, prompt: 'Where does current START?' to scaffold thinking
After completion, emphasise: 'It's a complete LOOP — any break stops all current flow!'
Use the LED variant after teaching Section 3.2.4 about making an LED glow
Use the switch variant after Section 3.2.6 about electric switches
Challenge mode (no hints) works well as a quick formative assessment
